### SUMMARY

This draft Review provides data on production and trade of tropical forest products and the status of tropical forests in ITTO member countries, as well as an overview of production and trade statistics of all timber products in these countries. Data are presented up to and including 2024, based on estimates made in the third quarter of that year. These estimates will be updated when data for 2024 is provided by member countries. The base year for analysis is 2023 as this is the latest year for which reliable data for most countries were available at the time of preparation. Statistics comparing tropical to all primary wood product production and trade, by volume and value, for 2023 and 2024, are given in Tables 1.1 and 1.2 for the 76 ITTO members (including the EU-27) and for the world. Secondary processed wood products (SPWPs) are not differentiated in trade statistics by species or source of raw materials. Tables 1.3 and 1.4 provide SPWP trade by value for 2023 and 2024 for all SPWP trade which includes both tropical and non-tropical wood products for many countries.

##### 1 Global economic trends 2023-2024

Global economic growth slowed in 2023 following a rebound in 2022 from the impacts of the COVID-19 pandemic which had resulted in production stoppages and disruptions in global supply chains over the previous two years. In 2023, growth had been impacted by the longer-term effects of the pandemic and the war in Ukraine, weak growth in productivity and geoeconomic fragmentation 1. Global economic recovery had also been affected by tighter financial conditions to lower inflation which had surged in response to pent up consumer demand accumulated during the pandemic and post-pandemic supply shortages, the withdrawal of fiscal support to curb high government debt, and persisting weakness in China’s property sector, a major wood products market. IMF’s World Economic Outlook estimates for 2023 show considerable divergence in economic growth between regions 1. In the United States, economic growth had strengthened in 2023, owing to robust consumption, government spending, and significantly reduced imports of goods and services. In contrast, growth in the euro area slowed sharply, with exports declining in response to a loss of export competitiveness amid high energy prices 2. Disruptions to shipping in the Red Sea from late 2023 caused disruptions to supply chains and pushed up shipping costs, particularly from Asia to Europe. China’s economic growth and recovery from the pandemic was slower than expected, with the property sector crisis and low consumer confidence constraining growth. These developments had significant implications for the global wood products sector, given China’s importance in the trade. In 2024, IMF’s latest forecast is for global economic growth to remain stable but low by historical standards, with geopolitical tensions posing a risk to the resilience of global supply chains, funding costs, cross-border capital flows and market efficiency. Economic growth could also be impacted by financial market volatility, trade policy uncertainty, the persistence of inflation, and natural disasters due to climate change. A major risk for the tropical wood product sector would be a deeper contraction in China’s property sector, which could weaken consumer sentiment and generate negative spillovers for the Asia-Pacific region and globally, given China’s large footprint in global trade 1. Weaker domestic demand from Chinese households and firms may result in more production focused on exports rather than domestic markets, and declining Chinese export prices would put pressure on profit margins of China’s competitors and potentially provoke retaliatory measures. In 2025 there will also be a heightened risk of trade protectionism in the United States which may

##### 2 Primary Wood Products Production

2.1 Tropical roundwood production 
The lack of reporting on production of tropical logs and other primary wood products by most of the major 
ITTO producer countries continues to limit the quality of production data available. Data estimates in this 
report are based on data provided by member countries in addition to data and anecdotal information from 
other sources. 
In the period 2020 to 2023, production of tropical industrial roundwood (logs) in ITTO producer member 
countries increased year-on-year from a low of 280.1 million m 3 in 2020 when industry lockdowns in 
response to the pandemic had temporarily disrupted supply chains and impacted production operations in 
many producer countries. By 2023, production totalled 289.3 million m 3, increasing slightly from the previous 
year but projected to remain at about the same level in 2024. In descending order, Indonesia, India, Viet Nam, 
Brazil, Thailand, and Malaysia accounted for about 83 per cent of total log production in 2023 and about 
78 per cent of production was in the Asia-Pacific region (Figure 1). Indonesia is ITTO’s largest producer by 
volume of tropical roundwood, which totalled 88.6 million m 3 in 2023. Although not reported in the Joint 
Forest Sector Questionnaire (JFSQ), anecdotal information suggests that the proportion of harvest from 
industrial plantations (particularly eucalypts, acacias, teak and rubberwood) in many ITTO Asia-Pacific 
producer countries has continued to grow in recent years, while the availability of logs from natural stands 
has fallen. 

The proportion of tropical roundwood to total roundwood production in ITTO member countries was 19 per cent in both 2023 and 2024, with ITTO member countries accounting for 87 per cent of world production of tropical logs. Significant non-ITTO producer countries, in descending order, include Nigeria, Uganda, Paraguay, Ethiopia, the Solomon Islands, Bangladesh, Lao PDR and Bolivia. In the African region, a significant proportion of production (55 per cent) is by non-ITTO member countries, whereas Asia-Pacific production is predominantly by ITTO members (97 per cent). Regional disparities in the rate of domestic conversion of primary products has continued, with Asia-Pacific, Latin America and Africa’s conversion of domestically produced logs to at least primary products averaging about 97 per cent, 93 per cent and 90 per cent respectively in 2023.
